name: Vylor

description: Vylor sells commercial seed to farmers around the world: corn, soybeans, sunflowers, wheat, canola, cotton and rice. The seed carries its own breeding (germplasm) and, for most corn and soybeans, patented gene traits for herbicide tolerance and insect or disease protection that Vylor either owns or licenses in. Farmers buy new seed every season, so revenue follows planted acres, the seed price per bag and how much of the crop uses Vylor's newest traits. The flagship Pioneer brand is sold mostly through its own direct sales agents, and Brevant seeds go through retailers. Vylor is also shifting from paying royalties on others' traits to earning royalties by licensing its corn and soybean traits to rival seed companies; it targets royalty-neutral in 2026 and a net royalty income of $1.0 billion by 2035. About 75% of sales and nearly all profit land in the first half of the calendar year, when the northern hemisphere plants.

corporateActions.text: Spun off from Corteva (CTVA) on Oct 1, 2026: Corteva's seed business, including Pioneer, with one Vylor share for each Corteva share. Joined the S&P 500 the same day.

employees.note: Approximately 12,300; about 73% in the Americas and 27% in Rest of World; about 11% represented by unions and works councils (information statement, 'Employees')

businessLines.name: Americas
businessLines.how: Farmers buy seed bags every planting season, mostly through Pioneer agents who sell direct (agency model) and through retail and cooperative channels for Brevant and other brands; the price per bag carries a premium for yield and trait technology. Growing royalty income also comes from licensing Vylor's corn and soybean traits to other seed companies, tied to their seed sales.
businessLines.description: Seed sales in North America, Latin America (Brazil, Argentina) and the rest of the Americas, led by United States corn and soybeans.

operatingProfit.note: Up 16% from $2,422M in FY2024; margin 35.7% (derived: 2,813 / 7,885). Share of the two segments' combined EBITDA of $3,413M: 82.4% (derived).

businessLines.name: Rest of World
businessLines.how: Same seed-bag model as the Americas, sold under Brevant and local brands to retailers, distributors and farmers; pricing and value capture on sunflower, corn and seed-applied technologies are the main lever.
businessLines.description: Seed sales in Europe, the Middle East and Africa (corn and sunflower, plus rice and millet) and Asia Pacific (India corn, Pakistan).

operatingProfit.note: Up 5% from $573M in FY2024; margin 29.8% (derived: 600 / 2,013). Share of the two segments' combined EBITDA: 17.6% (derived).

businessLines.name: Corn seed (product line across both segments)
businessLines.how: Annual hybrid seed sales under Pioneer (flagship), Brevant and local brands, plus trait royalties; new traits (multi-disease-resistant gene-edited corn, short-stature corn, triple-stack out-licensing) are the growth levers.

revenue.note: FY2024 $6,496M; FY2023 $6,447M. Product-line split is from the Corteva note on the Seed segment, whose net sales ($9,898M) equal Vylor's.

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $6,496M; FY2023 $6,447M. Product-line split is from the Corteva note on the Seed segment, whose net sales ($9,898M) equal Vylor's.

businessLines.name: Soybean seed (product line)
businessLines.how: Pioneer Z-Series and other soybean varieties carrying the Enlist E3 herbicide-tolerance trait; in Brazil it is moving to an out-licensing model, which swaps seed sales for royalty income.

businessLines.name: Other oilseeds (sunflower, canola and similar; product line)
businessLines.how: Seed sales of sunflower, canola and related oilseed hybrids, mostly in Europe, the Middle East and Africa; canola is also being developed as a biofuel feedstock crop.

businessLines.name: Other (wheat, cotton, rice, sorghum, silage inoculants and other; product line)
businessLines.how: Seed and related product sales in smaller crops; hybrid wheat is the planned next large crop, with a first commercial hard red winter wheat product targeted for North America as early as 2027.
